subject: pirate spider
title: This Spider Walks Into Other Spiders' Webs and Eats the Owner

scenes.text: Most insects fear spider webs. One spider walks in on purpose.
Pirate spiders hunt only one kind of prey: other spiders.
It creeps onto the web and plucks the silk, faking the struggle of a trapped insect.
The owner rushes over for a meal. The pirate bites its leg.
Its venom seems tuned for spiders and works almost at once, while long spines hold the victim.
Then it eats the owner's eggs too. The trap was the web all along.

description:
Pirate spiders (family Mimetidae, usually 3 to 7 mm long) invade the webs of orb-weavers and cobweb spiders and pluck the silk to mimic trapped prey, or sometimes a courting male.
When the resident arrives they bite it on the leg with fast-acting venom that seems specialised for spiders, and they also open and eat egg sacs.
Would you rather be the pirate or the web owner?
thumbnail_text: IT FAKES A MEAL TO BECOME ONE
first_comment: Sometimes it goes wrong and the web owner eats the pirate instead. Who would you bet on?
